memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses heard the people of every family wailing, each at the entrance to their tent. The Lord became exceedingly angry, and Moses was troubled. He asked the Lord, "Why have you brought this trouble on your servant? What have I done to displease you that you put the burden of all these people on me?" — Num 11:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here we see a great man of God completely worn out. Moses is not sinning grandly here — he is simply crushed. The endless wailing of a discontented people has pushed him to the edge, and he pours out his exhaustion honestly before God.

There is something deeply comforting in this. Moses does not pretend to be fine. He does not put on a brave face for God. He asks the raw questions we are often afraid to voice: "Why is this happening to me? What have I done to deserve this weight?"

If you are in a season of carrying too much — caring for aging parents, leading a struggling team, holding a family together, serving in ministry until you are hollow — Moses shows you that God can handle your honesty. You are allowed to tell Him you are at your limit.

But notice where Moses takes his frustration: to God, not away from Him. His complaint is really a prayer. And God, as we will see, responds not with rebuke but with practical help. Our God is gentle with the weary. Jesus Himself said, "Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest." The breaking point is not the end; it can be the place where God meets you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What burden have you been carrying that feels too heavy right now?
2. Are you being honest with God about your exhaustion, or hiding it?
3. What would it look like to bring your breaking point to Jesus?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am tired, and You already know it. Thank You that I can be honest with You. Help me to lay my heavy burden at Your feet and find rest in Christ. Amen.
